subject: Mutual plan: performance heatmap, variant tradeoffs & close timeline
messages:
From: Nina Patel <nina.patel@nexahealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: michael.chen@nexahealth.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual action plan & perf targets for triage prototype

Marissa / Redwood team —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. We're excited to move the triage prototype toward a production pilot. Before we lock a MAP and procurement timeline, I need a concrete performance evaluation plan and early numbers so my engineering and procurement teams can sign off. Goal and constraints:

- Use case: real-time patient triage (short prompts, structured JSON outputs).
- Target SLAs: TTFT (time-to-first-token) <= 200ms median, p95 latency <= 350ms for 32-token responses, sustain 200 concurrent QPS at 95th percentile under a 2s SLO.
- Cost target: <$10 per 1k inference tokens (ballpark for initial deployment).
- Data: we can provide a 50k sample of anonymized prompts and 2 hours of production traces.

Please send a proposed MAP with: evaluation plan (synthetic vs trace-driven workload), exact metrics to capture, hardware profile recommendations (dedicated v. hosted), model variant comparisons (quality/perf tradeoffs), and an accelerated close timeline (we're aiming to be purchase-ready mid-June).

I've attached a short questionnaire with our constraints and procurement notes (nexa_map_questions.xlsx).

Thanks —
Nina Patel
PM, NexaHealth
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@nexahealth.com>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan & perf targets for triage prototype

Hi Nina —

Appreciate the clear targets. Draft MAP + evaluation plan attached (MAP_draft_Nexa.pdf). High-level summary here so your team can review quickly:

1) Evaluation approach
  - Phase A (trace replay): run 2 hours of your production traces to validate tail latency and TTFT under realistic prefixes.
  - Phase B (stress grid): synthetic sweeping of concurrency (1, 8, 32, 64, 128, 200) and prompt length (8/32/128 tokens) to map throughput and degradation modes.
  - Phase C (quality check): run a shared eval set (5,000 prompts) across selected variants for precision/recall and hallucination checks.

2) Metrics to capture (per-run & aggregated):
  - TTFT median / p95 (ms)
  - Token throughput (tokens/sec) and effective requests/sec
  - End-to-end latency p50/p90/p95 (for streaming vs non-streaming modes)
  - Concurrency saturation point and graceful-degradation behavior
  - Cost estimate (token compute + network) per 1k tokens at measured throughput

3) Candidate model variants (we'll test these initially):
  - Variant X: redwood-7b-pt-8bit (compact, lower-cost)
  - Variant Y: redwood-xl-13b-q4 (best balance of perf/quality)
  - Variant Z: redwood-30b-fp16 (higher quality, higher resource needs)

4) Schedule (proposed)
  - May 24–25: baseline trace replay (Phase A)
  - May 26–27: stress grid (Phase B)
  - May 28: quality eval and internal review (Phase C)
  - May 30: MAP sync + recommendation for canary and procurement path

5) Deliverables
  - Raw traces + run configs (CSV/ZIP)
  - Consolidated perf heatmap (latency/throughput/TTFT) and recommended config per SLA
  - Mutual action plan with milestone dates and procurement checklist

If the proposed schedule looks good I'll coordinate with engineering to run the grid next week. Attachment: MAP_draft_Nexa.pdf.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: nina.patel@nexahealth.com
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Mutual action plan & perf targets — preliminary benchmark results

Team / Nina —

We ran the Phase A/B grid on a dedicated p4d-equivalent instance set and collected traces. Attached: nexa_benchmark_results_v1.csv (summary rows) + profile_traces.zip (kv/cache profiles). Quick interpretation below — numbers are medians across 3 runs unless noted. All runs used 32-token target answers and batching tuned to 24ms buff window. Costs are infra-only compute estimates per 1M tokens.

Summary (32-token responses):

Variant X — redwood-7b-pt-8bit
  - TTFT median: 85 ms
  - TTFT p95: 160 ms
  - p95 end-to-end latency: 320 ms
  - Tokens/sec per GPU: 4200
  - Sustained concurrency before p95 > 350ms: ~120 qps
  - Estimated cost per 1M tokens: $6.8
  - Quality notes: solid precision on short prompts; higher rate of partial-answer truncation on rarer entities (~2.8% failure on eval set)

Variant Y — redwood-xl-13b-q4
  - TTFT median: 110 ms
  - TTFT p95: 210 ms
  - p95 end-to-end latency: 280 ms
  - Tokens/sec per GPU: 6800
  - Sustained concurrency before p95 > 350ms: ~210 qps
  - Estimated cost per 1M tokens: $9.6
  - Quality notes: best balance of intent accuracy and low hallucination rate (0.7% on eval set)

Variant Z — redwood-30b-fp16
  - TTFT median: 190 ms
  - TTFT p95: 360 ms
  - p95 end-to-end latency: 440 ms
  - Tokens/sec per GPU: 9500
  - Sustained concurrency before p95 > 350ms: ~260 qps (but TTFT p95 breaches target)
  - Estimated cost per 1M tokens: $18.2
  - Quality notes: highest factuality on edge cases; marginal improvements vs Y on production eval (~0.5% absolute)

Operational notes:
  - Streaming-enabled requests reduce median TTFT by ~20–30ms across variants but p95 dynamics similar.
  - Prefix caching on common prompts reduced effective compute by ~12% in trace replay.

Attachment: nexa_benchmark_results_v1.csv, profile_traces.zip

I'll prepare a perf heatmap visualization for the MAP sync on May 30. Quick recommendation: Variant Y meets Nexa's throughput and quality targets with comfortable headroom for 200 qps and stays close to the TTFT goal (median 110ms).

-Karthik
Sr. Inferencing Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Nina Patel <nina.patel@nexahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Chen <michael.chen@nexahealth.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan & perf targets for triage prototype

Thanks Karthik — this is very helpful. A few clarifying questions before our May 30 sync:

1) TTFT median of 110ms for Variant Y is within our median goal, but p95 TTFT 210ms is higher than our 200ms target. Is there a practical tuning path (e.g., smaller batching window, different routing) to get p95 under 200ms without sacrificing quality?

2) For concurrency numbers: you report sustained concurrency ~210 qps before p95 > 350ms for Variant Y. Given our SLO of 2s, we actually can tolerate p95 up to 2s, but we need the TTFT SLO to remain tighter. Can we run a quick canary (1 week) in our account with 20% traffic to validate tail behaviour under real-world distribution?

3) Procurement: procurement wants a recommended SKU and a proposed purchase order by June 15 to hit their quarter deadline. What SKU do you recommend (Dedicated pool size / instance sizing) for an initial committed capacity to sustain 200qps with 1.5x buffer?

If you can address (1) and propose a canary/PO timeline in the MAP at the sync that would help us move fast.

-Nina
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@nexahealth.com>
Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 16:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan: performance heatmap, variant tradeoffs & close timeline

Nina / Michael —

Thanks for the quick turn. Summary and final MAP decisions from today's sync (attached: MAP_final_Nexa.docx) — short bullets so procurement can move:

Decisions & rationale
- Recommended variant for pilot: Variant Y (redwood-xl-13b-q4). Rationale: best balance of TTFT, sustained throughput, and quality; cost sits under your stated target (~$9.6 / 1M tokens) and gives ~1.05x headroom for 200 qps in our Dedicated config.
- TTFT tuning: to bring p95 TTFT closer to 200ms we will: 1) reduce batching window to 12ms for low-latency tier, 2) enable hot-cache pinning for top 5 prefixes observed in your traces, and 3) route critical calls to a lower-concurrency isolation pool. We estimate p95 TTFT drop of ~25–35ms from these ops (we will validate during canary).
- Canary plan: 1-week incremental canary (20% traffic), start date June 1 (provisioning May 31). Canary goals: TTFT p50/p95, error rate, downstream correctness sample.
- Procurement recommendation (SKU): Dedicated-XL-2 (2 x 8-GPU nodes capacity equivalent) with autoscale to +1 node burst. This supports ~4200 tokens/sec per node for Variant Y and meets the 1.5x buffer requirement.

Timeline (mutual action plan final):
  - May 31: Provision Dedicated-XL-2 pool (Redwood ops)
  - June 1–7: Canary (20% traffic)
  - June 8–10: Canary review & remediation window
  - June 11: Final sign-off for production ramp (if canary met KPIs)
  - June 15: Target date for PO submission (Nexa procurement)

Deliverables for procurement: pricing sheet, SOC2 evidence packet (if needed), DocuSign PO link. I've added the DocuSign and HubSpot record links in the MAP doc. Link: https://docusign.net/exec/ABC123

Next steps (owner)
  - Redwood (Marissa): finalize MAP doc and send DocuSign PO template by May 31 (done — MAP_final_Nexa.docx attached).
  - Redwood (Karthik): run targeted p95 TTFT tuning during provisioning window (May 31) and report results by June 2.
  - Nexa (Nina/Michael): confirm PO owner and internal sign-off timeline by May 28 (procurement requested earlier but accepted the June 15 backstop).

If approved I will circulate the final MAP and generate a HubSpot deal note (DEAL-4729).

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP_final_Nexa.docx
